reuse.why: Fintegra linking goes through the existing linkBankSyncAccount and link.findOrCreateBank, and all six providers share one new guard; the takeover reset re-writes unlinkAccount's field reset instead of sharing it.

duplication.why: The eight-field unlinked-state db.updateAccount block copies the one in unlinkAccount, and downloadFintegraTransactions is another copy of the per-provider download boilerplate (a pattern the tree already repeats).

placement.why: The guard sits in accounts/app.ts although the tree has accounts/link.ts for link helpers, and it bundles the closed-account check into a function named assertBankAccountIsNotLinked.

scope.why: Changes cover the four requested behaviours (guard, Fintegra provider, closed-account rule, takeover) without unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: One guard and one link core keep providers consistent, but the guard's name no longer describes what it checks or returns, and the unlinked-state field list lives in two places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: linkBankSyncAccount clears the replaced account with its own db.updateAccount reset instead of reusing the local part of unlinkAccount (accounts/app.ts).

disguised_duplication.where: The copied reset and the Fintegra download function are recognisable verbatim copies, not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountIsNotLinked gained replaceExistingLink plus a folded-in closed-account branch, and the shared linkBankSyncAccount gained replacedAccountId with its own reset branch; all six providers call both consistently.
